eligibility.quote: Then FCU confirms this with GPS_GLOBAL_ORIGIN message containing the same coordinates as LLA. But plugin transforms it to ECEF and sends to topic `mavros/global_position/gp_origin`.

missed_conditions.quote: gps_global_origin: remove LLA to ECEF conversion

loudness.quote: When I send a request containing LLA, I expect to receive a response containing LLA too in order to compare it and ensure that global_origin has been successfully set.

resolution.quote: gps_global_origin: remove LLA to ECEF conversion

notes: ELIGIBILITY DISAGREE. The spec stops at E2 step 2 ('internal') claiming 'no interaction between two units failed; the value crossing the interface is valid'. I read the failure differently: the plugin publishes gp_origin in ECEF while the message type geographic_msgs::GeoPointStamped declares LLA (WGS 84). The wrong coordinate frame crosses the gp_origin topic boundary to the consumer (the reporter's client, a separate node that sends set_gp_origin and reads gp_origin), which interprets the fields per the type and gets ECEF instead of LLA. Per S1_specify E2 step 2, 'A wrong value, frame, unit ... that crosses the boundary is an interface failure even when the resolving edit is inside one unit.' PR #1942 title 'gps_global_origin: remove LLA to ECEF conversion' and body 'However the messages are published in ECEF coordinates.' confirm the frame/representation crossing. Commenter lopsided98: 'I just ran into this as well and agree that it is very confusing and probably wrong to use ECEF in a GeoPoint.' So the case is eligible (stop_step 6), operation PAIR (gp_origin topic), interface kind topic; the missed condition is frame_mismatch (representation_convention is the close alternative). Loudness silent_documented / run (no build/connect/activate diagnostic; the reporter finds the wrong value by comparison). Resolution recommended: the fix PR is merged (commit 20c15364) but the issue thread shows no reporter re-run confirming the resolved composition working, so not observed.
